images.title: A pattern that goes down
images.purpose: Show a pattern that subtracts the same number each step and passes below ten thousand, so it changes from 5 digits to 4 digits.
images.composition: A rule banner on top and a chain of 6 boxes in two rows that turns at the right end and comes back along the second row.
images.exact_structure: Plain white frame, 1456 by 816. Top centre: a rounded banner reading Rule: subtract 1,000 in bold dark text (70 px) on a pale amber fill (tint of #E69F00) with a thin dark outline. Top row of 4 rounded boxes, left to right, each about 230 by 120 px with a thin dark outline, a pale blue fill (tint of #0072B2) and its number in bold dark numerals (52 px): 13,050, 12,050, 11,050, 10,050. Between neighbouring boxes of this row 1 straight dark arrow pointing right (3 arrows), each with the label −1,000 above it (U+2212 minus). Second row of 2 boxes, with a pale reddish purple fill (tint of #CC79A7): 9,050 directly below 10,050, and 8,050 to its left, directly below 11,050. 1 straight dark arrow points down from 10,050 to 9,050 with the label −1,000 beside it, and 1 straight dark arrow points left from 9,050 to 8,050 with the label −1,000 above it. 5 arrows in all. A small tag 5 digits sits above the box 10,050 and a small tag 4 digits sits under the box 9,050 (36 px, dark).
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: If the numbers fall, the rule takes away the same number each time, even when the numbers drop below ten thousand.
images.description: Boxes 13,050, 12,050, 11,050, 10,050 in a top row and 9,050, 8,050 in a second row joined by arrows each marked −1,000, with the banner Rule: subtract 1,000 and the tags 5 digits and 4 digits.
images.context: Concept image for Patterns that go down or cross ten thousand. It follows the two-row chain of boxes of your maths book and uses the video's own example, 13,050 down to 8,050.
images.teaching_notes: The numbers fall, so the arrows take away. Point at the step from 10,050 to 9,050, where the number loses its fifth digit. The last two boxes are the numbers the student writes next.

image_decisions.why: A two-row chain that goes down and crosses ten thousand shows a falling pattern and the change in digits.
